title: Run a script on a schedule with a LaunchAgent plist
summary: Write a small settings file that tells macOS to run your script every set number of seconds or at a set time, then load it. The script runs in the background under your user account, without a Terminal window.
prerequisites: A script file you can run with /bin/sh
The full path to the script, for example /Users/you/bin/backup.sh

steps.explain: Create the folder for your own launch agents if it is missing. The -p flag does nothing when the folder already exists.
List the agent files already in the folder. Choose a label that is not in this list. Creating a file with an existing name replaces that agent.
steps.expect: File names ending in .plist, one per line, for example com.example.backup.plist. The list is empty if you have no agents yet.

steps.explain: Create an empty XML property list file named after your label. This overwrites any file that already has that name.
steps.expect: No output. The file now exists and is empty.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

steps.explain: Store the agent name inside the file. launchd uses this Label key to identify the agent.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

steps.explain: Tell launchd what to run. /bin/sh runs your script, so the script does not need the execute permission. Use the full path to the script.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT_PATH
placeholders.description: Full absolute path to your script, starting with /Users. Not ~.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

steps.explain: Run the script every 3600 seconds, which is one hour. Change 3600 for another interval. Runs that fall while the Mac is asleep are skipped.
steps.expect: No output. Use only one schedule key: this one or the calendar key in the alternative.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

alternatives.explain: Run once a day at 09:00 instead of every N seconds. If the Mac is asleep at that time, the run happens after it wakes. Do not combine it with StartInterval.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

steps.explain: Optional. Write what the script prints to a log file, so you can see what happened on each run.

placeholders.name: LOG_FILE
placeholders.description: Full absolute path of the log file for the script output. Not ~.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

steps.explain: Check the file for syntax errors before loading it. A broken file cannot be loaded.
steps.expect: A line ending in ': OK' means the file is valid. Any other message names the problem, for example a missing value or an unknown type.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

steps.explain: Print the file in readable form. Check that Label, ProgramArguments and your schedule key are there and that the paths start with /Users.
steps.expect: A readable block listing the keys you set, such as Label, ProgramArguments, StartInterval and StandardOutPath, with their values. The layout can change between macOS versions.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

steps.explain: Load the agent into your user session. launchd then runs the script on the schedule. Do this only after the checks above pass.
steps.expect: Usually no output. If it prints an error, the file was rejected or the label is already loaded. Unload it with the rollback step, then run plutil -lint again.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

verify.expect: A block that starts with the service name and shows the program arguments and a state line, such as state = not running between runs.

rollback.explain: Unload the agent so the script stops running on the schedule.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

rollback.explain: Delete the settings file so the agent is not loaded again later.

placeholders.name: LABEL
placeholders.description: Unique agent name, reverse-DNS style. Also the plist file name without .plist. Must not match an existing agent.

warnings: Paths inside the plist must be full paths such as /Users/you/bin/backup.sh. launchd does not expand the ~ symbol.
plutil -create replaces any existing file with the same name. Check the list from ls ~/Library/LaunchAgents before you create a file.
The script runs in the background under your account, without a Terminal window. Test it by hand first, for example with sh followed by the script path.
A label can be loaded only once. Running the bootstrap step again for a loaded label fails. Unload it with the rollback step first.
The script runs unattended on every schedule tick. Keep it limited to what you need and avoid commands that delete files.
